summary.name: 青简输入法 Qingjian
summary.one_liner: Qingjian (青简) is a Rust-based Chinese Pinyin input method for macOS that shows an English or Japanese translation of each candidate word, so you pick up vocabulary while typing.
use_cases: learn english words while typing chinese
learn japanese vocabulary while writing chinese
offline pinyin input without uploading data
use shuangpin or fuzzy pinyin on macos
summary.what_it_does: Qingjian is a Chinese Pinyin input method written in Rust for macOS. It supports whole-sentence conversion using a small local model that reranks candidates, abbreviated pinyin, spelling correction, fuzzy pinyin, shuangpin, an English mode and emoji. Next to each candidate it can show a part-of-speech tag and a translation in English or Japanese (one language at a time); Japanese translations get hiragana readings over kanji. Words seen fewer than three times are shown in orange as new words and turn grey once familiar. The page says pinyin, lexicon, sentence model, learning and definitions all run locally with no network calls, while an optional user-configured AI provider can be used for word and sentence completion, asking questions about characters, and translating selected text.
notable: Learning translations shown inline in the candidate window, one language at a time, with new words highlighted in orange
Core input (pinyin, lexicon, sentence model, learning) runs fully on-device with no network access
Rust-based; listed on awesome-mac under Input Methods as open source and freeware
caveats: Platform support named on the page is macOS only, though the awesome-mac listing describes it as cross-platform
Optional AI features require the user to supply their own AI provider
Learning language is limited to English or Japanese, and only one is active at a time
